facts.claim: Prime Minister Ali Faleh al-Zaidi ordered the cancellation of three leases at Mosul International Airport over alleged connections to armed groups; the November 7 decision affects seven passenger check-in counters, an airport car park and a taxi office.
Iraqi authorities have not identified the armed groups allegedly connected to the companies or published evidence supporting the claims.

All three leases were signed by the Iraqi Airports Administration on behalf of the Transport Ministry, each covering an initial three-year period with an option for renewal, according to contract documents obtained by Shafaq News.

Sky Plus, registered in the United Arab Emirates, leased seven check-in counters covering 42 square metres; Sama Al-Matar leased an uncovered parking area of 4,228 square metres; Basra-based Al-Faisal Al-Shamikh operated a four-square-metre taxi office in the arrivals hall.

Nineveh Governor Abdul Qader al-Dakhil said the Transport Ministry and airport administration concluded the contracts without consulting provincial authorities, and said he had taken legal action against former Transport Minister Razzaq Muhaibis al-Saadawi and the airport administration.

Al-Zaidi instructed officials to accelerate plans for specialised international companies to participate in operating and jointly managing the airport; no replacement companies have been announced and no timetable has been provided.

Mosul International Airport was heavily damaged after Islamic State militants seized the city in June 2014; reconstruction began in August 2022, the rebuilt facility was inaugurated on July 16, 2025, and Iraqi Airways operated the first passenger flight to Baghdad on November 6, 2025, after an 11-year interruption; the airport has a 3,000-metre runway and capacity for 630,000 passengers a year.

zh.title: 伊拉克取消摩蘇爾機場三項租約：疑涉武裝團體，改邀國際業者接手
zh.summary: 伊拉克總理下令取消摩蘇爾國際機場三家業者的租約，指其疑似與武裝團體有關連，但當局未指明團體身分、也未公開證據；三項租約涵蓋七座報到櫃台、停車場與計程車辦公室，政府計畫改由國際業者參與營運與共同管理。
body: 伊拉克正尋求以國際業者取代摩蘇爾國際機場的三家商業營運商。此前總理阿里·法萊赫·扎伊迪（Ali Faleh al-Zaidi）下令取消三項租約，理由是業者疑似與武裝團體有關連；決定於11月7日作出，涉及七座旅客報到櫃台、一座機場停車場與一間計程車辦公室，租約分別由Sky Plus、Sama Al-Matar與Al-Faisal Al-Shamikh持有。伊拉克當局未指明所涉武裝團體的身分，也未公開支持指控的證據。

據Shafaq News取得的合約文件，三項租約皆由伊拉克機場管理局代表交通部簽署，初期皆為三年、可續約。其中在阿拉伯聯合大公國註冊的Sky Plus承租航廈內42平方公尺的七座報到櫃台；Sama Al-Matar承租4,228平方公尺的露天停車場；總部位於巴斯拉的Al-Faisal Al-Shamikh則承租入境大廳內4平方公尺的計程車辦公室。取消決定也與租約授予方式的爭議有關：尼尼微省省長阿卜杜勒·卡迪爾·達希勒（Abdul Qader al-Dakhil）表示，交通部與機場管理局未諮詢省級當局便簽署合約，他已就此對前交通部長拉扎克·穆海比斯·薩達維（Razzaq Muhaibis al-Saadawi）與機場管理局採取法律行動。

總理同時指示官員加速推動專業國際業者參與營運、共同管理摩蘇爾國際機場；他曾於10月12日訪問摩蘇爾時邀請外國機場業者投資該機場。目前尚未公布接替業者，也未提供移交三項服務或選定國際機場管理夥伴的時間表。摩蘇爾國際機場於2014年6月伊斯蘭國武裝分子攻占該市後嚴重受損，重建於2022年8月展開，2025年7月16日由前總理穆罕默德·希亞·蘇達尼（Mohammed Shia al-Sudani）主持重新啟用；客運航班於同年稍晚恢復，2025年11月6日伊拉克航空執飛摩蘇爾至巴格達首班客運航班，為中斷11年後首次。重建後的機場擁有一條3,000公尺跑道，航廈設施設計年旅客容量63萬人次。

en.title: Iraq axes Mosul Airport leases over alleged armed group links
en.summary: Iraq is seeking to replace three commercial operators at Mosul International Airport with international companies after Prime Minister Ali Faleh al-Zaidi ordered their leases cancelled over alleged connections to armed groups. The authorities have not identified the groups or published evidence, and no replacement companies or timetable have been announced.
body: Iraq is seeking to replace three commercial operators at Mosul International Airport with international companies after Prime Minister Ali Faleh al-Zaidi ordered the cancellation of their leases over alleged connections to armed groups. The November 7 decision affects agreements covering seven passenger check-in counters, an airport car park and a taxi office, held by Sky Plus, Sama Al-Matar and Al-Faisal Al-Shamikh respectively. Iraqi authorities have not identified the armed groups allegedly connected to the companies or published evidence supporting the claims.

According to contract documents obtained by Shafaq News, all three leases were signed by the Iraqi Airports Administration on behalf of the Transport Ministry, each covering an initial three-year period with an option for renewal. Sky Plus, registered in the United Arab Emirates, leased seven check-in counters covering 42 square metres in the passenger terminal; Sama Al-Matar secured a lease for an uncovered parking area spanning 4,228 square metres, while Basra-based Al-Faisal Al-Shamikh was contracted to operate a four-square-metre taxi office in the arrivals hall. The decision also follows a dispute over how the agreements were awarded: Nineveh Governor Abdul Qader al-Dakhil said the Transport Ministry and airport administration had concluded the contracts without consulting provincial authorities, and told local media he had taken legal action against former Transport Minister Razzaq Muhaibis al-Saadawi and the airport administration over the agreements.

Alongside the cancellations, al-Zaidi instructed officials to accelerate plans for specialised international companies to participate in operating and jointly managing Mosul International Airport; the prime minister had previously invited foreign airport operators to invest in the facility during a visit to Mosul on October 12. No replacement companies have been announced yet, and the government has not provided a timetable for transferring the three services or selecting an international airport management partner. Mosul International Airport was heavily damaged after Islamic State militants seized the city in June 2014; reconstruction began in August 2022, and the rebuilt facility was officially inaugurated on July 16, 2025, by former Prime Minister Mohammed Shia al-Sudani. Commercial passenger operations returned later that year: on November 6, 2025, Iraqi Airways operated the first passenger flight between Mosul and Baghdad after an 11-year interruption. The reconstructed airport features a 3,000-metre runway and terminal infrastructure designed to accommodate up to 630,000 passengers annually.
